messages:
maria: quick idea — propose a small 'validator plugin' interface for model onboarding. pluggable checks run in parallel and emit structured signals. goal: non-blocking by default, but policy can promote failures to blocking.
dan: +1. curious about ordering semantics and how we mark something as "fatal" vs advisory.
lee: thinking three phases: 1) fast sanity (schema, tokenizer), 2) async microbench (p95/p99 on small sample), 3) blocking compatibility (binary ABI, runtime). plugins declare phase.
sasha: propose a minimal plugin contract: name, phase, timeout_s, resources, run command, outputs (status, metrics), compatibility matrix. also a version field so we can evolve.
maria: example YAML to discuss in RFC:
```
name: kv-cache-smoke
version: v1
phase: microbench
timeout_s: 60
resources: {cpu: "0.5", mem_mb: 256}
run: "/opt/onboard/checks/kv_smoke --model $MODEL_PATH"
outputs:
  - status: pass|warn|fail
  - metrics: p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec
compatibility:
  - runtime: [tvm, cuda-12.1, cuda-12.3]
```
dan: nice. how do we surface warnings in console and console rollouts? i'd like a single aggregated score + per-plugin breakdown. warnings should be visible in Console > Onboards and in PRs.
sasha: aggregator idea — each plugin emits severity + weight. aggregator computes weighted score and also emits a small vector of failing plugin ids. policy config maps score thresholds to outcomes (allow, require human review, block).
lee: scaling note — heavy plugins (full microbench) should be run via job-pool with sampling. we should support sample rotation (rotate which inputs are used every N runs) to avoid overfitting the microbench.
maria: agreed. also we need provenance: store plugin outputs + input snapshot + binary hash in object store. attach artifact refs to the model registry entry.
eng-bot: bench-run queued for model rmdl-2023-07, job id 34291 — estimated 45s
dan: compatibility with quantized binaries — plugin should declare supported quantization formats and an interface to call the quantized runner. otherwise plugin can return 'inconclusive'.
sasha: also need stable plugin UIDs: plugin_name@semver so we can migrate configs when plugin behavior changes.
maria: next steps: write a short RFC that includes the contract YAML, aggregator behavior, sampling policy, storage schema, and a spike plan. propose spike owners: dan + sasha. lee to scope job-pool changes.
dan: i can pick up the aggregator spike. will prototype simple scoring function and a Console mock.
sasha: will sketch plugin adapter API and a default set of plugins (tokenizer, kv-smoke, golden-inference, runtime-abi).
lee: will draft the sampling rotation logic and job-pool admission control.
maria: cool. aim for a 2-week spike and then RFC follow-up. thanks all :party-parrot:
dan: thanks! :thumbsup:
eng-bot: noted assignees: dan, sasha, lee. created tracking ticket: ONBOARD-772
